blogs.title: Optimizing Web Performance: Slashing Page Load by 73% (11s → 3s)
blogs.excerpt: A hands-on breakdown of how we diagnosed main-thread bottlenecks, offloaded heavy computations to Web Workers, implemented list virtualization, and used surgical React memoization to slash initial page load from 11.2s down to 2.9s.
content: ## The 11-Second Bottleneck: Context & Challenge

When our engineering team took ownership of the real-time financial analytics platform, page load times were alarming. On initial load, users were stuck staring at skeleton screens for **nearly 11.2 seconds**.

The application had to ingest real-time WebSocket feeds of 10,000+ stock price ticks, calculate technical indicators (RSI, EMA, Bollinger Bands) on the fly, and display live data grids. Every single streaming tick was triggering cascading re-renders across parent containers, choking the main UI thread and causing severe frame drops during user scrolling.
## Step 1: Profiling First (No Guesswork)

Before writing a single line of optimization, we fired up the **Chrome DevTools Performance Profiler** and **React DevTools Profiler**. The timeline recordings quickly revealed two massive bottlenecks:

* **Main-Thread Saturation**: Mathematical transformations and array manipulations inside render cycles were producing continuous long CPU tasks (>450ms).
* **Monolithic Bundle Size**: Heavy charting modules (ECharts, Canvas renderers) and modal dialogues were statically imported into the root chunk, blowing the uncompressed bundle up to **3.8MB**.
* **Excessive DOM Mounts**: 500+ active table rows with live tickers and SVG sparklines were mounted simultaneously.
## Step 2: Feature-First Architecture & Shared Primitives

We started by restructuring the repository into a modular, domain-driven structure. This isolated feature logic and eliminated circular dependency trees:

* **`src/features/*`**: Self-contained domain modules (e.g. `orderbook/`, `stock-analytics/`, `portfolio/`).
* **`src/shared/*`**: Atomic UI building blocks (`Button`, `InputField`, `CardWrapper`, `Text`, `Chip`).
* **`src/workers/*`**: Dedicated Web Worker scripts isolated from the UI runtime.

This eliminated redundant component duplications and cut unused utility CSS by 35%.
## Step 3: Offloading Heavy Calculations to Web Workers

The highest-impact architectural win was moving compute-intensive indicator calculations off the main thread entirely.

We spawned a dedicated background Web Worker that ingests raw WebSocket ticks, computes the moving averages and technical indicators in the background, and returns formatted, display-ready data via structured cloning:
## Step 4: Windowed List Virtualization

Rather than mounting 500+ DOM nodes for active stock watchlists, we implemented **windowed virtualization** using `@tanstack/react-virtual`.

Now, regardless of whether a watchlist has 100 or 10,000 tickers, only the **18 rows currently in viewport** (+ 3 overscan rows) are ever created in the DOM tree:
## Step 5: Surgical Memoization (`useMemo`, `useCallback`, `React.memo`)

We ran a re-render audit and resolved prop instability across high-frequency components:

* **`useCallback`**: Wrapped event handlers to prevent passing new function instances on every tick.
* **`useMemo`**: Cached filtered collections, sort orders, and currency conversions.
* **`React.memo` with custom comparison**: Ensured child row components only re-render if their specific price or change percentage actually changed:
## Step 6: Code Splitting & Lazy Route Loading
## Real-World Results & Key Takeaways

After rolling these architectural upgrades into production, the benchmark improvements were dramatic:

* ⚡ **Initial Page Load**: Slashed from **11.2s → 2.9s** (**73% faster**)
* 🎯 **INP (Interaction to Next Paint)**: Reduced from **410ms → 32ms**
* 📦 **Active DOM Nodes**: Dropped from **4,200 → 320 nodes** (**92% reduction**)
* 🚀 **Frame Rate**: Steady **60 FPS** during volatile real-time market data surges

> **Core Rule**: Never optimize on intuition alone. Profile first with DevTools, shift heavy compute off the main thread with Web Workers, virtualize high-density UI lists, and maintain strict referential stability across your React component tree.

blogs.title: Building Real-Time Event-Driven Architectures with Kafka, Redis & WebSockets
blogs.excerpt: How to scale sub-second market data streaming and event processing across microservices using Kafka message queues and Redis pub/sub.
content: When delivering real-time updates to tens of thousands of concurrent users, traditional HTTP polling collapses under server load.
We break down our event-driven architecture pairing Apache Kafka for resilient, durable message ingestion and Redis Pub/Sub for low-latency WebSocket client distribution.
This architecture guarantees message order, handles burst traffic without dropping packets, and delivers sub-second client updates.

blogs.title: Integrating Agentic AI Chatbots into Production Web Applications
blogs.excerpt: Lessons learned collaborating with ML teams to bridge conversational agentic workflows with typed UI components and secure database query execution.
content: Modern users expect intelligent natural language query interfaces rather than static multi-level filter menus.
In this post, we discuss how we built an Agentic AI chatbot allowing conversational data queries with strict authorization barriers and deterministic JSON output schemas.
